none: The poem and gloss concern rainwater and praise of a woman's mouth; shared wording with 22:18 is incidental.
The passage is an aging and bereavement poem; it does not gloss the wording of 28:81.

words: وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqī reads a Banū Asad poet's denial of perfect generosity as modest self-praise and cites 34:24 as a tactful way to present one's own and another's positions.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب قوله عز وجل: " وإنا أو وإياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال ". وهذا كلام من نظر لنفسه وغيره

none: The gloss concerns reproach and a horse's usefulness in danger; its connection to 80:18 is incidental.
The passage mourns lost brothers and the passing of time; it does not gloss 84:13.
The passage glosses a camel and its strength; it does not bear on 84:13.
The passage is a biographical account of Ṭarafa's relation with his brother, with no gloss on 7:11.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zawzanī explains the line as a cow fearing that either space between her legs may be the locus of danger, so she cannot tell which way to flee.
rows.anchor: يقول: فغدت البقرة وهي تحسب أن كلا فرجيها مولى المخافة، أي موضعها وصاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zawzanī says كلا is singular in form but dual in sense, while كل is singular in form despite its collective sense; 19:93 illustrates agreement by form, alongside 18:33 and 27:87 as contrasts.
rows.anchor: ونظير كلا وكلتا في هذين الحكمين كل؛ لأنه مفرد اللفظ وإن كان معناه جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet reports a sweeping claim that everyone who performs the act under discussion is their ally, then says he is their ally; al-Zawzanī says the line's ending has the same sense under every reading of العير.
rows.anchor: قوله: وأنا الولاء، أي أصحاب ولائهم، فحذف المضاف، ثم إن فسر العير بالسيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If العير means a lord, the claim is that all who approve killing Kalib b. Wa'il are their cousins and the blood-feuds attach to the poet's group as allies.
rows.anchor: ثم إن فسر العير بالسيد كان تحرير المعنى: زعم الأراقم أن كل من يرضى بقتل كليب وائل بنو أعمامنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If العير means a wild ass, all hunters of wild asses are called their allies, extending the guilt of a particular group to the public.
rows.anchor: وإن فسر بالحمار كان المعنى: أنهم زعموا أن كل من صاد حمر الوحش موالينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If العير means a tent peg, everyone who pitches tents is called their ally, extending one group's guilt to the Arabs at large.
rows.anchor: وإن فسر بالوتد كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من ضرب الخيام وطنبها بأوتادها موالينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If العير means a mote, everyone who stirs motes aside to clear water is called their ally.
rows.anchor: وإن فسر بالقذى كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من ضرب القذى ليتنحي فيصفوا الماء موالينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If العير means a particular mountain, everyone who reaches that mountain is called their ally.
rows.anchor: وإن فسر بالجبل المعين كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من صار إلى هذا الجبل موال لنا

rows.speaker: عبد يغوث بن وقاص الحارثي
rows.claim: In his plea to Banu Taym for clemency, the poet says their brother was not among his بوائيا, using the same negated-category construction as 7:11.
rows.anchor: أمعشر تيم قد ملكتم فأسجحوا ... فإن أخاكم لم يكن من بوائيا
